title: Controlplane upgrade sequencer with hypothesis-driven smoke validation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement an upgrade sequencer for Private (VPC) control plane versions that coordinates Terraform hooks, synthetic/hypothesis-driven smoke validation, and safe rollback. The goal is an automated, tenant-aware canary flow with drift detection and automated fallback so operator intervention is required only for complex failures. Deliverables: 1) terraform module hooks and version manifest support; 2) sequencer service (controller) that applies cohorts, triggers smoke hypotheses, evaluates telemetry, and decides promote/rollback; 3) smoke validation suite (synthetic requests + invariants) with threshold dashboards; 4) runbook and a minimal UI in the console for manual override and rollout status.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules expose pre-upgrade and post-upgrade hook endpoints and reconcile version manifest per-tenant
Sequencer can run a 5% tenant cohort promotion and automatically evaluate smoke hypotheses against metrics (latency P95, 5xx rate, controlplane reconciliation errors)
Sequencer triggers automatic rollback when hypothesis failure rate > 30% within evaluation window or when drift detector flags terraform drift
Smoke suite reproducibly validates control-plane API surface (create/delete/open session, RBAC checks) with <25s end-to-end latency in canary cohort
Dashboards show cohort-by-cohort telemetry and the sequencer exposes a /status API for progress and decision rationale
Runbook documents manual mitigation steps and postmortem checklist for upgrade regressions
design_notes: Spike showed hypothesis-driven approach reduces false positives compared to single-metric gating
Prefer a lightweight sequencer running in controlplane operator cluster (binary + leader-election) rather than a centralized orchestrator to reduce cross-tenant blast radius
Terraform hooks use a callback URL that the sequencer implements; we persist a version manifest in S3-like storage per deployment for auditable history
Cohort membership is tenant-fractionation based and deterministic to support retryability
Decision engine uses weighted rules: primary metrics (P95 latency, 5xx rate) + reconciliation errors + drift score. Weighting configurable per-release
implementation_plan: Week 1: Terraform module changes, manifest format v1, hook schema, and unit tests
Week 2: Sequencer prototype (apply -> wait -> run smoke -> evaluate) and local e2e harness
Week 3: Integrate synthetic smoke suite and telemetry ingest (prometheus metrics + traces)
Week 4: Canary policy configurator, dashboards, /status API, and initial runbook draft
Week 5: Internal dogfood on non-critical tenant subset, iterate thresholds, and produce launch checklist
risks: Terraform drift detection could be noisy; will need heuristics to avoid spurious rollbacks
Synthetic smoke flakiness if test clients are not isolated from noisy downstream services
Operator trust: automated rollback could interfere with long-running migrations if not gated properly
Network callback delivery for terraform hooks needs retries and idempotency to avoid double-promotions
mitigations: Implement exponential-backoff and idempotency tokens for hook callbacks; sequencer to dedupe events
Run smoke suite in isolated test namespaces and use mocked dependencies where realistic
Add a migration-aware hold state: sequencer recognizes tagged tenant migrations and excludes them from auto-promote
Expose a safe-mode that requires human approval for first 3 releases of a given major version
